content:
As per tradition, the Apple Store has gone down ahead of today's September Apple event, set to begin at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time.

We expect Apple to announce the all-new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, the foldable iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12, and an updated AirPods (5th generation).

This marks the first event led by new CEO John Ternus, who will unveil multiple new products, including the debut of the foldable iPhone Duo.

The Duo features an outer display of approximately 5.5 inches when folded and around 7.8 inches when unfolded—slightly smaller than the iPad mini. Its large unfolded screen delivers an immersive media experience and supports split-screen multitasking, allowing two apps to run side by side.

Apple is widely expected to differentiate its foldable from competitors by focusing on premium craftsmanship, including a custom-designed hinge. The crease on the inner display is expected to be very subtle.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are also set to be announced today, featuring a new processor, an improved camera system, and an all-new cherry red colour option. The Dynamic Island on the new Pro models is said to be narrower, with further reduced bezels. The 18 Pro lineup is widely expected to see a starting price increase of around US$100.

The standard iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will not be appearing at today's event. Apple is adjusting its launch schedule, so the entry-level iPhone will no longer debut in the fall and is instead expected to arrive in the spring. In the meantime, Apple is expected to continue selling the standard iPhone 17.

Additionally, a new Apple Watch lineup is expected to be unveiled today, including the Series 12 and Ultra 4, along with the new AirPods 5. The new Apple Watch is reported to feature innovative health-tracking capabilities and a new AI feature that generates summaries of users' daily activities and conversations.

Other upcoming Apple hardware includes a smart home display product, a redesigned Apple TV and HomePod mini, and a MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen. Most reports indicate these products will launch later this year, likely as part of an October event.

9to5Mac is on the ground in Cupertino today, bringing you live coverage of all the iPhone announcements—stay tuned for the latest updates.
